steps.label: Do Now: The Clock (1 of 3)
steps.content:
Do Now: The Clock (1 of 3)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does "State the name of this component" want a name, and not a description?Show the answer

State asks for a short answer. The name alone earns the mark, so a long description wastes time.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2023, Question 3(c). A computer has a central processing unit (CPU).

Total: 1 mark

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: the beat

steps.text: A similar idea. A band plays to a beat. One player keeps the beat, and everyone plays one note on each beat.
steps.visual: beat, beat, beat: one note each

steps.text: A faster beat means more notes in each minute. Everyone plays faster, but each note is the same.
steps.visual:
slow beat: 60 notes a minute
fast beat: 120 notes a minute

steps.text: The CPU works the same way. One component sends out a regular pulse. On each pulse, one FDE cycle is done.
steps.visual: pulse, pulse, pulse: one FDE cycle each

steps.text: More pulses each second means more FDE cycles each second.
steps.visual: pulses per second = cycles per second

steps.text: Your question asks for a component, not a speed. So give the name of a part of the computer.
Your question: which component sends out those pulses? It sets how many cycles happen in one second.
steps.visual: the one that keeps the beat

steps.label: Do Now: Cache (2 of 3)
steps.content:
Do Now: Cache (2 of 3)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy test every option in a multiple choice question, not just pick the first one that sounds right?Show the answer

Several options can sound right. Testing each one against what you know finds the one that is fully true.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2025, Question 2(c)(i). The computer has primary storage. One example of primary storage is cache.

Total: 1 mark

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: test each statement

steps.text: A similar question. Which statement describes the purpose of a register? A: it stores data for many years. B: it stores data temporarily, inside the CPU.
steps.visual:
A: for many years?
B: temporarily, inside the CPU?

steps.text: Test each statement against what you know. A register loses its value when the power goes off, so A is wrong. B fits.
Watch for a statement that describes a different part. Ask: is this the job of this part, or of another part?
steps.visual: the right job, for the right part

steps.text: Cache is a small store very close to the CPU. Getting a value from it is faster than going out to RAM.
steps.visual:
CPU ↔ cache: fast
CPU ↔ RAM: slower

steps.text: Cross out each statement that is wrong, and say why in a few words. The one left must be fully true.
steps.visual: cross out, then check the one left

steps.text: Your question: test all four statements the same way. Which one says why cache makes the CPU faster than going to RAM each time?
steps.visual: test A, B, C and D one at a time

steps.label: Do Now: Instruction Sets and Embedded Systems (3 of 3)
steps.content:
Do Now: Instruction Sets and Embedded Systems (3 of 3)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does a "State what is meant by" question want a kind of thing first?Show the answer

Saying what kind of thing it is, then what makes it different, gives the examiner a full meaning in one line.

Part (a): Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, June 2024, Question 5(b). Instructions are processed by a central processing unit (CPU) in a computer. Part (b): Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, November 2024, Question 6(a). A computer program is created for an embedded system in a washing machine.

Total: 2 marks

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: instruction sets and embedded systems

steps.text: A similar question. State what is meant by a character set.
Say what kind of thing it is, then what is in it, then who uses it.
steps.visual: a list ... of all the characters ... a computer can represent

steps.text: Your part (a): use the same pattern. It is a list. A list of what? Which part of the computer can carry them out?
steps.visual: a list + of what + by what

steps.text: A similar question. State what is meant by a general purpose computer.
Say what kind of thing it is, and what makes it different: it can perform many different tasks, such as a laptop.
steps.visual: a computer ... that can perform many different tasks

steps.text: Your part (b): an embedded system is the other kind. How many tasks does it do? Where is it found: on a desk, or inside a machine?
steps.visual: how many tasks + where it is

steps.label: Check Your Notes: Performance, Instruction Sets, Embedded Systems
steps.content:
Check Your Notes

3 minutes. Tick each fact you have. Add anything missing in a different colour.

  • Clock speed: the number of FDE cycles per second. Higher means more instructions each second.
  • Cores: each core can process instructions at the same time as the others.
  • Cache: small, fast memory in the CPU for data and instructions used often.
  • Instruction set: the list of all the commands a CPU can process.
  • Embedded system: a computer system built into a larger device to do a dedicated function.
  • Embedded features: dedicated hardware, a microprocessor, firmware, cannot easily be reprogrammed.
  • General purpose computer: can do many different tasks, such as a laptop.
Think → Pair → ShareWhy add missing facts in a different colour?Show the answer

The new colour shows what you did not know. Learn those parts first.

steps.label: Performance: Clock Speed
steps.content:
Performance: Clock Speed

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is "it makes the computer faster" not enough for 3 marks?Show the answer

It is one general idea. The marks need the steps: what the clock speed is, what changes, and the effect.

4 minutes. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2025, Question 5(c). Data is processed by the central processing unit (CPU) in a computer that has a Von Neumann architecture.

items.prompt: Explain how the clock speed can affect the performance of a CPU.
items.modelAnswer: The clock speed is the number of FDE cycles performed per second. If it is increased, more FDE cycles are performed each second, so performance improves.
scheme: on each clock pulse, an FDE cycle is performed
the clock speed is the number of FDE cycles performed in a second // the number of times the clock pulses per second
if clock speed is increased more FDE cycles can be performed in a second // if it is decreased fewer FDE cycles can be performed in a second
if clock speed is increased, it can improve the performance of the CPU // if it is decreased, it decreases the performance
items.context: 4 minutes. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2025, Question 5(c). Data is processed by the central processing unit (CPU) in a computer that has a Von Neumann architecture. Question: Explain how the clock speed can affect the performance of a CPU. Marking rule: Three from, one mark for each point met, up to 3.

steps.label: Embedded Systems: The ATM
steps.content:
Embedded Systems: The ATM

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does "it is a computer" earn no mark in a question about embedded systems?Show the answer

Every computer is a computer. A mark needs a feature that only an embedded system has.

4 minutes. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2025, Question 4(b). An automated teller machine (ATM) is a device where a person inserts their bank card and can request to withdraw money. The ATM also allows the person to check how much money they have in their bank account.

items.prompt: Describe the features of the ATM that identify it as an embedded system.
items.modelAnswer: It has a dedicated function. It has a microprocessor.
scheme: dedicated function // special purpose device // not general purpose device
dedicated hardware // by description, for example hardware is only used for ATM functions
contains microprocessor // does not have CPU
items.context: 4 minutes. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2025, Question 4(b). An automated teller machine (ATM) is a device where a person inserts their bank card and can request to withdraw money. The ATM also allows the person to check how much money they have in their bank account. Question: Describe the features of the ATM that identify it as an embedded system. Marking rule: Any two from, one mark for each point met, up to 2.
